question: The brothers Sidhu and Kanhu were the leaders of which of the following tribal uprisings?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Santhal Rebellion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sidhu** and **Kanhu Murmu** were the leaders of the **Santhal Rebellion** (1855–1856), one of the most significant tribal uprisings in India.
 
• The rebellion took place in the **present-day states of Jharkhand, Bihar, and West Bengal**. It was a response to the exploitation and oppression faced by the Santhal tribe under the **British colonial rule** and moneylenders, landlords, and revenue officials.
 
• The Santhal community was subjected to **high taxes, exploitation, and forced labor**, which led to widespread dissatisfaction and ultimately resulted in the rebellion.
 
• The **rebellion started in 1855** when Sidhu and Kanhu, along with their brothers Chand and Bhairav, mobilized the Santhal community to fight against the British authorities and landlords.
 
• The Santhals declared independence from British rule and waged war against the British army and landlords. This rebellion is considered one of the earliest expressions of organized resistance against colonial exploitation in India.
 
• Although the rebellion was eventually suppressed by the British forces in 1856, it left a lasting impact on the tribal identity and struggles for justice in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Santhal Rebellion:**

 
 
• The rebellion was triggered by the exploitation of the **Santhal community** by **zamindars (landowners), moneylenders, and British officials** under the colonial system.
 
• The Santhals were forced to pay exorbitant taxes, and their lands were seized by landlords, leading to widespread impoverishment and oppression.
 
• Sidhu and Kanhu mobilized the community to rise against the oppression, leading to the **declaration of rebellion in June 1855**.
 
• The Santhal Rebellion is also known as the **Hul Rebellion**, where "Hul" means revolution in the Santhal language.
 
 
 
• **Other Tribal Uprisings:**
 
 
• **Koya Revolts:** These revolts occurred in the **Godavari region of Andhra Pradesh** and were led by the tribal leader **Alluri Sitarama Raju**. They were against the exploitation and restrictions imposed by the British.
 
• **Kol Mutiny:** This uprising took place in **Chota Nagpur (present-day Jharkhand)** in 1831–1832. It was led by the Kol tribes against the British and moneylenders exploiting their land and resources.
 
• **Ho Uprising:** The Ho tribe in **Singhbhum region (present-day Jharkhand)** revolted against the British, landlords, and exploitative policies in 1820–1837.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Santhal Rebellion:**
 
 
• The rebellion led to **increased awareness** about the plight of tribal communities and their exploitation under colonial rule.
 
• It resulted in the introduction of laws like the **Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act (1876)**, which aimed to protect the rights of the Santhals over their land and resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Sidhu and Kanhu:**

 
 
• Sidhu and Kanhu were **charismatic leaders** who united the Santhal community to fight against British colonial oppression.
 
• They aimed to establish a society free from exploitation and oppression, inspiring future tribal movements in India.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Santhal Rebellion remains a symbol of tribal resistance and courage. It is commemorated in the tribal regions of India as a significant historical event.
